title: Whose Side Are You On? A Framework and Benchmark for Assessing LLM Political Stances through Politicians Social Media Posts
abstract: arXiv:2611.34098v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly participate in political discussions, making it important to understand which positions they support or oppose. We propose a framework for assessing LLMs' political stances through simulated social media interactions. The framework uses politicians' posts and multiple prompting methods to identify consistently expressed stances. Using this framework, we construct WorldPOLL, comprising 4,600 political posts from X/Twitter collected from approximately 200 politicians representing ruling and opposition blocs across 23 countries. Our quantitative analysis shows how support and opposition vary across models, countries, and political directions, while our qualitative analysis identifies the political views and policies models support or oppose. translated_title: 你站在哪一边？一个基于政客社交媒体帖子评估大语言模型政治立场的框架与基准
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）越来越多地参与政治讨论，因此理解它们支持或反对哪些立场变得十分重要。我们提出了一个通过模拟社交媒体互动来评估LLM政治立场的框架。该框架利用政客的帖子和多种提示方法来识别LLM持续表达的立场。基于这一框架，我们构建了WorldPOLL数据集，其中包含从X/Twitter收集的4,600条政治帖子，这些帖子来自代表23个国家执政与反对阵营的约200名政客。我们的定量分析展示了支持与反对在不同模型、国家和政治方向之间的变化，而定性分析则识别出模型支持或反对的具体政治观点和政策。这些分析共同揭示了各模型之间的共同立场以及不同国家背景下的差异。我们还考察了模型是否表达一致的立场。
tldr: 该论文提出了一个通过政客社交媒体帖子模拟互动来评估大语言模型政治立场的框架，并构建了覆盖23个国家约200名政客共4,600条帖子的WorldPOLL基准，揭示了各模型间的共同立场与不同国家背景下的差异。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a framework and the WorldPOLL benchmark (4,600 posts from ~200 politicians across 23 countries) for assessing LLM political stances through simulated social media interactions, revealing shared positions across models and differences across national contexts.
